key_insight: Imperfect PDE knowledge improves regression convergence rates only below a modeling-error threshold; with exact physics, studied PDE classes yield rates corresponding to dimension d−1 rather than d.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify when physical constraints can improve data efficiency and provide conditions for near-linear estimator computation and tuning without knowing the modeling error.
method: Benchmark physics-informed regression against regression using only smoothness assumptions.
Derive modeling-error thresholds for all linear PDEs and certain nonlinear PDEs.
Establish minimax-optimal rates up to logarithmic factors for classes of constant-coefficient elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence rates and minimax guarantees, but describes no empirical datasets or experiments.
watch_item: The detailed rate guarantees cover specific PDE classes, and near-linear computation requires additional conditions.
paper_title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
